title: Tinkerbench — prompt scrapheap and few-shot rescue attempts
content:
Notes to self: rough, noisy, meant to be iterated.

Goal: harvest a small set of resilient few-shot templates for user-facing summarization and instruction-following in the new small-window product. Must: be short, predictable, and degrade gracefully when context truncated.

Quick experiments (model: small-open-v2, temp=0.2 unless noted):

1) Minimal instruction template (baseline)
Prompt: "You are a helpful assistant. Summarize the following text in one paragraph. Text: "<INPUT>""
Expectation: concise, neutral-tone.
Failures observed: when input has bullets, model returns list instead of paragraph ~45% of runs. Token budget wasted with leading restatement.
Mitigation attempts: force-format line -> "Output: paragraph only. No bullet points." helps but sometimes repeats phrase "As a summary".

2) Few-shot rescue (3-shot) — anchor + counterexample
Shots:
- Good: short news paragraph -> correct summary
- Bad: bulleted list -> model converted to paragraph (explicit example)
- Edge: long rambling email -> summary retains key actions
Template: Instruction + 3 shots + "Now summarize: <INPUT>"
Results: improves paragraph-only outputs to ~82%. But hallucination of non-existent dates increases slightly.

3) Constraint-first framing (experiment)
Prompt: start with explicit constraints: "Do not introduce facts not present. Single paragraph. Max 60 words. Avoid phrases like \"As a summary\"." Then one-shot example.
Observation: strongly reduces hallucinations; however, sometimes truncates important qualifiers. Need dynamic max-words tied to input length.

Failure cases catalog (examples copied from logs):
- When input contains a question and then context, model answers the question rather than summarizing the whole. (Example tokenized snippet: "Q: Are we shipping? Body: ...")
- Lists -> outputing bulleted list despite instruction.
- Redundant preambles: "In summary, ..." repeated.
- Tone drift: legalese -> overly informal summary.

Hypotheses + fixes: 
- Hypothesis: model uses early tokens to decide output format; moving constraints after shots sometimes ignored. Fix: place constraints both before and after shots (redundancy).
- Hypothesis: short temperature increases randomness; but at low temp model still repeats framing. Fix: set top_p=0.95 for diversity patch.

Recipe candidates (doable in product):
- Core template: constraints header (2 lines) + 2-shot examples (good/bad) + dynamic length heuristic + final instruction line.
- Fallbacks: if model returns bullets, run light post-processing heuristic to stitch into paragraph (join with ". " and dedupe lead phrases).

Token budget notes: 3-shot adds ~120 tokens to prompt. For high-volume endpoints this is nontrivial. Consider: canonicalize shots to extremely compact examples (one-sentence inputs/outputs) to shave 60% of shot cost. Also evaluate prefix caching for the constraint+shots block.

Quick checklist before shipping a template:
- [ ] Works on small-open-v2 and mid-open-v1 with same prompt (no model-specific hacks)
- [ ] Passes 90/100 on paragraph-only format on held-out test set
- [ ] Hallucination rate < 3% (entity/date hallucinations)
- [ ] Token cost per request within budget target for tier (calc attached in linked sheet)
- [ ] Edge-case handling: questions-in-input, nested lists, code blocks

Open questions / TODOs:
- Try constraint repetition + example inversion (place counterexample after correct example) — does order matter?
- Test compact-shot designs: can binary-form examples (labelled GOOD/BAD in 6 tokens) achieve parity?
- Should we pre-process inputs to normalize lists (convert bullets to paragraph) before sending? Tradeoff: loses fidelity for structured outputs.

Scratch examples (do not copy to final):
- Compact 2-shot: "GOOD: \"AI reads the paragraph and returns one-sentence summary.\" BAD: \"AI returns bullets.\" Instruction: <INPUT> => Summary:
- Observed output: often begins with "Summary:" which we want to strip.

Debug snippets (for logs):
- Slack thread ref: #prompt-tinker — threads 145-147 (see linked artifact above).
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-templates/pull/312 (compact shots branch).

My immediate next steps (this week):
1) Build 2 compact-shot variants (A/B) and run 5k queries on small-open-v2.
2) Implement quick post-process stitcher for bullet->paragraph and estimate latency impact.
3) Draft short playbook entry for console team: recommended templates + when to use fallback.

If anyone picks this up: please copy this doc into shared_drives/engineering/developer-experience/ and add notes under a new section "playbook drafts" so we can iterate with design and console infra.

Random notes to self: sometimes model obeys instruction better when constraint text includes an explicit negative ("Do not X") rather than a positive one ("Only X"). Keep that pattern.

End of scrapheap — salvage what looks promising.
